standard_prerequisites.name: Loop space of a pointed type
standard_prerequisites.statement: Omega(A,x) is the pointed type of loops at x, and Omega f is the induced map of loop spaces.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the object of the second hypothesis and of the commuting square in the proof.

standard_prerequisites.name: Theorem 8.8.1 (truncated Whitehead, base case)
standard_prerequisites.statement: If trunc 0 f is surjective and ap f is an equivalence on all path spaces then f is an equivalence.
standard_prerequisites.use: It reduces the goal to showing that ap f is an equivalence, which is the first line of the proof.

standard_prerequisites.name: Two-out-of-three property for equivalences
standard_prerequisites.statement: If two of three maps in a commuting square of equivalences are equivalences then so is the third.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is applied to the displayed square at the end of the proof.

core_obligations: Reduce by the retained Theorem 8.8.1 to proving that ap f : (x = y) -> (f x = f y) is an equivalence for all x, y : A (source line 2407).

Use the equivalence-inhabited-codomain result to assume a path in B, so that trunc 0 (f x) = trunc 0 (f y), and exploit that trunc 0 f is a bijection to obtain trunc(-1)(x = y) (source lines 2408-2409).
Since the goal is a mere proposition, assume an actual path p : x = y (source line 2410).
Display the commuting square comparing Omega(A,x) and (x = y) with Omega(B, f x) and (f x = f y), whose horizontal maps are concatenation with p and with f(p) (source lines 2411-2419).

Conclude that ap f is an equivalence because the other three maps are: the two horizontal ones by the equivalence of concatenation, and the left-hand one by hypothesis, so two-out-of-three applies (source lines 2420-2421).

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce to ap f being an equivalence by Theorem 8.8.1.
Strip the two truncations to obtain an actual path p.
Compare loop spaces through the commuting square and apply two-out-of-three.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Corollary 8.8.2 at source lines 2398-2405: f is an equivalence as soon as trunc 0 f is a bijection and Omega f is an equivalence at every point. The author's proof (source lines 2406-2422) is a reduction that consumes four separate results in a specific order: Theorem 8.8.1 turns the goal into the statement that ap f is an equivalence (line 2407), the equivalence-inhabited-codomain result allows one to assume a path in the codomain (line 2408), the bijectivity of trunc 0 f then yields a truncated path between the points (line 2409), and after stripping that truncation one displays a square comparing loop spaces with path spaces through concatenation (lines 2411-2419) to which the two-out-of-three property is applied, the left-hand vertical map being the hypothesis and the horizontal maps being equivalences by the concatenation lemma (lines 2420-2421). The statement mentions only the two hypotheses and the conclusion.
